speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are here to discuss your acute diarrhea. To begin our evaluation, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and have you noticed any blood or mucus in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent treatment with levofloxacin for pneumonia, it is highly concerning that you developed severe watery diarrhea with cramping. This pattern strongly suggests a *C. difficile* infection. Are you currently experiencing fever, and have you noticed any dehydration symptoms like dizziness or decreased urination?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Watery diarrhea. I also have Lower abdominal discomfort, Abdominal cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Levofloxacin-associated Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI).

I will order a stool test to confirm the diagnosis and determine the need for immediate treatment. REQUEST TEST: C. difficile Toxin EIA. REQUEST TEST: Stool O&P exam.
